Sizing workshop objectives (what customer needs):
- Baseline QPS: determine steady-state QPS vs peak QPS (customer reports steady 6 QPS, predictable marketing spikes to 22 QPS for promotional events).
- Tokens/sec planning: average 140 tokens/request translates to baseline tokens/sec requirement at steady-state ~840 tokens/sec and peak ~3080 tokens/sec. Need GPU mapping (tokens/sec per H100/A100) + headroom.
- Latency SLOs: target p95 <= 300ms for support chat (preferred) and p99 <= 800ms; product-search reranking can tolerate higher latency up to p95 600ms. Need routing policies for different classes.
- Throughput guarantees & SLA: customer requires committed throughput during sales events and credits for missed SLOs; legal wants 99.9% availability + regional residency commitments.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask = recommendation for committed pool. Early engineering estimate: 4-6 H100s to handle steady-state with autoscale for peaks; workshop to produce concrete per-model GPU counts, batching knobs, and KV cache sizing.
- Fallback & graceful degradation: define model fallbacks (quantized variants) and routing to hosted pool as emergency fallback.

POC/Benchmarks so far:
- Small POC run on hosted with 2x smaller model: peak test (30s sustained) reached 35 QPS but p95 rose to 1.2s — shows need for dedicated optimized kernels & batching.
- Customer provided traces (Drive link) that we'll use to build token distributions and simulate.
